title: 🐉 Motion Trail

accepted_baseline.label: Full-stamp old-redraw
preserve: BASE remains available as variant 1 and must not be visually rewritten
color image rather than black line art

current_candidate.summary: ORBIT/LOOP now render a deterministic worm/dragon body instead of a historical trail. Each body segment samples the exact same hairpinPose() path as the head at pathDistance - offset. Body length is 26/32/38 segments by quality with 20/18 px spacing (~520–684 px), the artificial sine wave is removed, and the black endpoint tapers to ~16% temporal scale.

accepted_asset_direction: 2 WINGS is the current favorite and primary visual reference
real color imagery rather than black line art on white
creepy masks, faces, creatures, strange objects and winged/open forms
strong eyes, horns, ritual/iconic presence are desirable when the silhouette remains readable
open_feedback: Review whether ORBIT/LOOP now reads as one long worm/dragon body rather than a short trail.
Confirm every body segment visibly takes the same turns as the head, with no independent wobble or shortcut.
Review whether ~684 px body length at high quality is enough or should extend farther around the racetrack.
Review the 16% black endpoint taper and body spacing (18 px normal / 20 px reduced-motion).
Review performance on target phone; ORBIT/LOOP now avoid historical stamp creation/aging and use mostly one draw per old segment.
Some masks still need cleaner segmentation: remove gray base/residue/halo before promotion.
resolved_feedback_in_current_candidate: 2 WINGS remains available and is now the default displayed variant.
1 BASE remains available with its accepted full-stamp rendering preserved.
Removed MANTIS/DRAGON/MOTH/OCTO/SKEL line-art direction from the promoted comparison set.
Added four color creepy Japanese mask candidates with strong faces/horns/eyes.
All six production assets live under visuals/trail-lab/assets and runtime performs no external image fetch.
BASE and WINGS were localized using build-time processing that reproduces their previous runtime treatment.
Mask backgrounds were segmented to alpha before promotion; production runtime does not draw museum/background rectangles.
No abrupt horizontal mirror/flip was reintroduced; current six variants use fixed orientation.
Adaptive quality, bounded stamp pool, low internal resolution, high-cadence full stamps and rebound accumulation were preserved.
Portrait mobile exposes all six numbered variants in a visible 3x2 grid.
Added visible in-page NOTES documenting the reusable Trail architecture and current iteration lessons.
Added pseudo-3D modes without changing asset-specific code: CERCA, LEJOS, ÓRBITA and LOOP add z depth to the same stamp records.
Kept 2D as the accepted full-stamp bounce mode.
Depth rendering uses projection and far-to-near ordering while preserving the bounded stamp pool.
No WebGL, mesh or per-image 3D implementation was introduced.
Old/rear copies now render much darker and brighten progressively toward the current head, addressing the double-face effect when a 3D trajectory turns.
3D distance adds extra darkening to far stamps while the current head remains full-strength.
Darkness is precomputed into seven shaded sprite canvases once per asset load; runtime does not apply expensive per-stamp CSS/canvas filters.
Added smooth 2.5D vertical-axis yaw driven by z velocity.
When returning toward camera, the sprite reopens smoothly; no abrupt horizontal mirror/flip is introduced.
Each historical stamp captures its own yaw so trail copies preserve the orientation they had when created.
2D mode remains visually unchanged with yaw fixed at 0.
Rearward motion no longer makes the sprite disappear.
At profile, the sprite crosses into a horizontally mirrored rear representation while width is near zero, avoiding a visible snap.
The mirrored rear side stays darker and slightly more transparent than the front.
Historical stamps preserve their captured yaw and therefore preserve front/profile/rear orientation history.
2D remains unchanged.
Stamp intervals increased from 24/28/34 ms to 30/35/42 ms across high/medium/low quality.
Trail lifetime increased from 720 ms to 860 ms (reduced-motion 880→1040 ms), making the visible tail longer while keeping the pool bounded.
Removed the independent distance-gated yaw accumulator from 3D turning.
The retreat straight starts only after yaw reaches 180°; the next approach straight starts only after yaw returns to 0°.
Approach mode starts at yaw 0° and Retreat mode starts at yaw 180°, so neither begins with a late orientation correction.
The previously approved longer/spacier trail cadence and lifetime remain unchanged.
ORBIT/LOOP no longer use smoothstep/time easing for path progression.
A single pathDistance advances by PATH_SPEED × dt (230 px/s normal, 150 px/s reduced-motion).
Hairpin turns use a 64-sample ellipse arc-length table so distance, not phase percentage, controls turn progress.
The oldest trail stamp now maps to brightness 0 and therefore uses a literal black precomputed silhouette.
Existing depth projection still compounds the far/rear size reduction naturally.
Replaced the flattened screen-space hairpin with a broad semicircle in the X/Z plane.
Turn radius is responsive and substantially larger: 130–230 px, based on viewport width/height.
Constant PATH_SPEED is preserved; larger radius naturally takes longer because the path itself is longer.
Removed whole-sprite abs(cos(yaw)) width collapse from 3D rendering.
Added curved-surface strip projection using 7/9/11 slices by quality level.
At side yaw the curved surface retains visible thickness instead of collapsing to a near-zero-width sheet.
Near face-on views still use a single image draw for performance; strip rendering activates mainly while turning.
Removed pseudo-3D yaw/depth transparency: trail pieces remain solid; only source-image alpha defines cutout edges.
Pseudo-3D brightness recovers faster than scale so the dark tail is concentrated near the true endpoint rather than making the whole body muddy.
Pseudo-3D stamps are emitted by travelled distance (12px normal / 14px reduced-motion), keeping spacing stable across frame-time variation.
Curved strip rendering is limited to the head and newest ~18% of the trail.
Older small/dark stamps use one drawImage with a 30% side-profile width floor, reducing draw calls substantially.
2D accepted cadence/hierarchy remains on its prior time-based path.
Removed the artificial tail sine offset from ORBIT/LOOP.
ORBIT/LOOP no longer render historical stamps as the body.
Each body segment is a delayed sample of the exact same hairpinPose() trajectory used by the head.
Adaptive body length is 26 / 32 / 38 segments with 18px normal spacing (20px reduced-motion), reaching ~684px at high quality.
The final black tail endpoint now tapers to ~16% temporal scale.
ORBIT/LOOP avoid stamp creation and stamp aging entirely; body state is preallocated and recomputed from path distance.
2D remains the accepted historical-stamp baseline; CERCA/LEJOS retain their distance-stamp history.

asset_localization_evidence.alpha_check: all six generated assets reported transparent corners [0,0,0,0]; mask assets reported 22.7%–36.3% near-transparent pixels; BASE/WINGS 48.4%/67.7%

mask_direction_review.note: User said the masks are much better and liked the mask direction, but some masks still show gray/base residue or insufficiently clean cut edges.

engine_architecture.projection: pseudo-3D focal projection; no WebGL required
optimization: single loaded sprite reused for all copies
preallocated 40-slot deterministic dragon body for ORBIT/LOOP
ORBIT/LOOP do not create/age historical stamps
body segments are recomputed directly from the cached trajectory function
curved 7–11 slice renderer limited to head/newest body only
old dark/small body segments use one drawImage each
visual_hierarchy: oldest trail stamp brightness is exactly 0 (black silhouette)
oldest trail stamp scale starts at 56% before additional far-depth scaling
brightness and scale rise together toward newest trail stamp
farther 3D depth additionally reduces both visual dominance and projected size
shade bank is precomputed once per asset load; no per-stamp runtime filter

yaw.driver: trajectory phase; no independent yaw accumulator
behavior: approach mode is front-facing from the start (yaw 0°)
retreat mode is rear-facing from the start (yaw 180°)
ORBIT/LOOP near hairpin holds z at near depth while x crosses laterally and yaw advances 0→180°
the backward straight begins only after the hairpin completes, with yaw already 180°
far hairpin holds z at far depth while x returns laterally and yaw advances 180→0°
rear proxy remains mirrored/darker and never disappears

trail_spacing.intent: slightly wider spacing plus longer lifetime to make the trail visibly longer without losing complete-stamp identity

trajectory_turn.geometry: true semicircle in x/depth-equivalent metric; no flattened screen-space ellipse
trajectory_turn.loop_vertical_lift: optional constant-metric vertical lane transition during each semicircle
trajectory_turn.key_rule: turn radius is large and speed stays constant; retreat begins only after yaw reaches 180°

surface_curvature.model: 2.5D curved image surface using vertical strips
surface_curvature.side_profile: retains curved-surface thickness at 90° yaw instead of collapsing to near-zero scaleX
surface_curvature.rear: source strip order reverses on rear hemisphere; rear brightness hierarchy remains
surface_curvature.optimization: straight/front/rear views use one draw call when near face-on; strip rendering is used mainly during turn

dragon_tail.model: deterministic delayed samples of the same head trajectory
dragon_tail.cheap_tail_renderer: older small/dark segments use one drawImage with thick side-profile floor

pseudo3d_review.note: User said the previous tail was too short and still read as a trail. Required worm behavior: every tail segment must follow exactly the same path as the main face, only delayed along that path.
